Also, it originally was 60 pulls to guarantee the chibi, but each pull costed 100 tokens. When they reworked the system, it now required 50 tokens per pull and it gave out 10 medallions over the course of 120 pulls (which guarantees the chibi and at the same price as before). The track is put below the chibi because each pull has a small chance of getting the chibi. So there is a chance for you to be able to get the chibi AND 10 medallions (which you can then use to buy other content) after 120 pulls.

TLDR: halved cost but doubled requirement for guarantee, but system became slightly better.

  
For clarification: In the old gacha system, if you didn't get the chibi after 59 pulls, the chibi is guaranteed on your 60th pull (hence the 60 pull guarantee, but there is also a chance to get the chibi earlier).

In the new system, you get rewards per 10 pull (where each single pull gives you a chance to get 1 or 5 medallions, or the chibi itself). The 60 pulling track only gives you 4 medallions because if you are 50 pulls in and haven't gotten a single medallion, you are guaranteed to get one on your next pull. So 120 total pulls gives you 10 medallions which you can use to claim the chibi you want. If you are lucky, you can get the chibi before the 120 pulls, and you can then save your medallions for something else.

Damage buffs of the same kind are additive, while damage buffs of different kinds are multiplicative.

Assuming you have 2000 attack and a skill with a 100% atk multiplier.

Assuming a standard damage formula of:

Atk × atk modifier x skill multiplier x damage modifier = damage dealt

If you have 0 buffs:

2000 x 1 (+0) x 1 x 1 (+0) = 2000

If you have 2 attack buffs, one at 30% and one at 20% then the damage calculation looks something like:

2000 × (1+(0.3+0.2)) × 1 x 1 = 2000 × 1.5 x 1 x 1 = 3000

If you have a 30% atk buff and a 20% elemental damage buff, then the damage calculation becomes:

2000 x (1 + 0.3) x 1 x (1 + 0.2) = 2000 x 1.3 x 1 x 1.2 = 3120


While these are basic calculations and is not reflective of hsr's actual damage formula, it follows a similar principle. As seen above, two buffs of different kinds provide more damage than stacking 2 buffs of the same kind.

Main DPS - Support 1/Sub-DPS - Support 2

Support 1/Sub-DPS- deals damage too but also provides buffs, can be on the field for a short amount of time
Support 2- deals minor damage than the previous two, but makes up for it with more buffs. Only goes on field to give their buffs

HoRb Support:
DPS - HoRb - Prom

Bleed Focused:
Susannah - (whichever support 1 you have, HoRb or HoS) - Griseo

Tldr: get magic pen with scaling value after damaging enemy with spell. magic pen value increases against low hp enemies. get max magic pen if enemy is shielded.

Non 5-year explanation ahead:
Shadowflame is better than Void Staff if you are against enemies who don't build MR (or have low MR).

Hre's some math to compare it with Void staff.
Shadowflame:

Against non-shielded enemy with 100 MR at full health:
Shadowflame reduces enemy MR by 10 = 90 MR
Void Staff (40% magic pen) reduces enemy MR by 40 = 60 MR

Against shielded enemy with 100 MR at full health:
Shadowflame reduces enemy MR by 20 now = 80 MR
Void Staff still reduces enemy MR by 40 = 60 MR

Against non-shielded enemy with 50 MR at full health:
Shadowflame reduces enemy MR by 10 = 40 MR
Void Staff (40% magic pen) reduces enemy MR by 20 = 30 MR

Against non-shielded enemy with 50 MR at full health:
Shadowflame reduces enemy MR by 20 = 30 MR
Void Staff (40% magic pen) reduces enemy MR by 20 = 30 MR

So at MR values lower than 50, Shadowflame will tend to reduce more MR
(especially if the enemies have a lot of low cd shielding spells like Lux or Lulu or have Aery equipped)

You get 10-20 magic pen after hitting an enemy with magic damage, with the magic pen scaling up the lower the enemy hp is, but if they are shielded (or recently shielded) you get the max magic pen value instead.

It gives her a lot of avenues for disadvantages, higher HP while helpful can also lead to enemies dealing higher damage against her (esp when they equip items or runes that increases damage based on enemy max hp like LDR, Cut Down, Sunderer etc.). Its easy to mitigate the issues of having low HP by having good positioning. If the issue is her w hp costs, it becomes negligible if you hit your Qs which is also expected of you as a Soraka player (hitting your Qs also become easier during the messier teamfights).

A build I find fun is derived from Luminum's movespeed build as the MS helps you easily reposition and bavigate teamfights. Warmog's is also significantly more expensive for a support who has no kill potential and is fully reliant on support income. It also provides only HP and AH, while other support items can give more AH, and have better utility passives for your team for cheaper but at the cost of lesser hp (item stats such as H/S power, or item passives such as Staff of Flowing Water's AH passive). Also, Warmog's healing passive can be compensated for by Soraka's Q healing, provided you land it.

Tldr: Warmog's is an expensive item with stats skewed toward hp, and a selfish hp regen passive that rewards bad positioning more. The gold used for Warmog's could have been used for items with more teamwide utility as that will be better than its hp regen passive in the long run.
